title: Apparent clash: “You know me” and “You know neither me nor my Father”
english: If the same hearers were addressed both by [[“You know me, and you know where I am from” >> Bible:John 7:28]] and by [[“You know neither me nor my Father” >> Bible:John 8:19]], the saying would look like a flat contradiction.

As it is, “You know me” is reported to certain Jerusalemites, while “You know neither me” is spoken to the Pharisees. The letter sharpens the knot: [[“Whoever denies the Son does not have the Father either.” >> Bible:1 John 2:23]]
translator_notes: OET. Pass A!=B. Heine not wording. Melito skipped. Never Cyril Matthew. Book 19 incomplete in MSS.

title: Sometimes as man, sometimes as divine nature one with the Father
english: Reply: the Savior sometimes speaks of himself as a man, and sometimes as of a more divine nature united with the Father’s unbegotten nature.
[[“You know me and know where I am from” >> Bible:John 7:28]] concerns his humanity; [[“You know neither me nor my Father” >> Bible:John 8:19]] concerns his deity.
translator_notes: OET. Pass A!=B. Heine not wording. Melito skipped. Never Cyril Matthew. Book 19 incomplete in MSS.

title: Heterodox misuse: not the demiurge’s Father?
english: One must know that the heterodox think this passage clearly proves that the God whom the Jews worshiped is not Christ’s Father.

They say so because they have not read the divine Scriptures or watched their idiom. Even [[Eli’s sons “did not know the Lord” >> Bible:1 Samuel 2:12]] — through wickedness, not because they missed some other god.
translator_notes: OET. Pass A!=B. Heine not wording. Melito skipped. Never Cyril Matthew. Book 19 incomplete in MSS.

title: Knowing God is not the same as bare believing
english: So much to show that being known of God is other than being merely believed on.
Knowing added to believing differs greatly: [[to one is given a word of wisdom, to another a word of knowledge by the same Spirit, to another faith by the same Spirit. >> Bible:1 Corinthians 12:8-9]]
translator_notes: OET. Pass A!=B. Heine not wording. Melito skipped. Never Cyril Matthew. Book 19 incomplete in MSS.

title: To know is to be united; Adam ‘knew’ Eve only after joining
english: See whether Scripture also calls those blended and united to something “knowing” that with which they were mixed. Before such union, even if they grasp words about it, they do not know it.

Adam saying [[“This at last is bone of my bones” >> Bible:Genesis 2:23]] did not yet “know” the woman; when he clung to her, [[“Adam knew Eve his wife.” >> Bible:Genesis 4:1]] And [[“he who clings to the Lord is one spirit.” >> Bible:1 Corinthians 6:17]]
translator_notes: OET. Pass A!=B. Heine not wording. Melito skipped. Never Cyril Matthew. Book 19 incomplete in MSS.

title: Can one know God and not know the Father? Same Creator is Christ’s Father
english: Next ask whether someone can know God and not know the Father. If “Father” and “God” are different aspects, perhaps one may know him as God without knowing him as Father.

Yet we have clearly learned that the Creator and God of the prophets, Father of Christ, is also God and Father of us — as Paul writes [[concerning his Son, who was descended from David according to the flesh. >> Bible:Romans 1:3]]

title: Pharisees lacked both knowledge and faith toward Father and Christ
english: So the Pharisees not only lacked knowledge of the lawgiver — neither as Father nor as God, the Father of Christ — they did not even believe him.
Nor did they know the Christ; the Savior rightly convicts them: [[“You know neither me nor my Father.” >> Bible:John 8:19]]
translator_notes: OET. Pass A!=B. Heine not wording. Melito skipped. Never Cyril Matthew. Book 19 incomplete in MSS.

title: From knowledge of the Son one ascends to the Father
english: I ask whether [[“If you knew me, you would know my Father also” >> Bible:John 8:19]] is equivalent to the converse, “If you knew my Father, you would know me,” or not.

I think they are not equivalent. One ascends from knowledge of the Son to knowledge of the Father: [[“Whoever has seen me has seen the one who sent me.” >> Bible:John 12:45]] It is impossible to behold God except by way of the Word.

title: These words spoken in the treasury; offerings as intelligible gift
english: [[These words he spoke in the treasury as he taught in the temple; and no one seized him, because his hour had not yet come. >> Bible:John 8:20]]
Since the common good is helped in two ways — by words and by the deeds the righteous do — those deeds too are well referred to the intelligible treasury.
translator_notes: OET. Pass A!=B. Heine not wording. Melito skipped. Never Cyril Matthew. Book 19 incomplete in MSS.

title: The poor widow’s two mites; God looks on the heart
english: But Jesus, according to Luke, looking up at the rich casting their gifts into the treasury, also sees [[the poor widow casting in two mites. >> Bible:Luke 21:2]]
Calling the disciples, he teaches them to look not as a human looks but as God looks: [[a human looks on the face, but God looks on the heart. >> Bible:1 Samuel 16:7]]
